# agent-spendcap

Budgets and semantic rate limits for AI agents. Zero dependencies. MIT.

## Install

npm i agent-spendcap

## What it does

Gives each agent scope a cost cap (USD), a tool-call cap, an external-write cap,
and named sliding-window rate limits (e.g. 5 financial actions per hour).
Check before every action, record after. check() is pure; record() mutates.

## Quickstart

import { createBudget } from "agent-spendcap";
const budget = createBudget({ maxCostUsd: 5, maxToolCalls: 50, rates: { refundsPerHour: 5 } });
const r = budget.check({ kind: "tool", costUsd: 0.02 });
if (!r.allowed) throw new Error(r.reason);
budget.record({ kind: "tool", costUsd: 0.02 });

## API

createBudget(config): { check, record, snapshot, reset }
config: maxCostUsd?, maxToolCalls?, maxExternalWrites?, rates? (name -> max per
window), rateWindowMs? (default 3600000), scope? (default "default"),
onExhausted? (fires at most once per dimension per reset), logJsonl?
(append-only audit path), now? (injectable clock).
check({ kind, costUsd?, rateKeys? }) -> { allowed, reason?, remaining }
kinds: "tool" | "financial" | "email" | "external-write".
Only kind === "external-write" counts toward the external-write cap.
record(usage) updates counters, appends { ts, scope, kind, costUsd, rateKeys }
to the JSONL log, fires onExhausted for newly exhausted dimensions.
snapshot() -> { spent, remaining, scope }. reset() zeroes counters and fired
flags; the JSONL log is never cleared.

## Pairs with

callgate (https://github.com/richardsondx/callgate): the gate decides whether
an agent SHOULD act; agent-spendcap decides HOW MUCH it may spend doing it.
